prompt: Review this anchor as its assigned subagent. Enumerate ALL requirements, qualifications, edge cases and scenarios. Inspect all supplied implementation and test fragments and trace each aspect to implementation behavior and actual test assertions or justified TODO/N/A evidence. Passing tests and associations alone are insufficient. Follow helpers and capture every additional source dependency with cargo meta review read ANCHOR PATH [selector] before completing the report. Explain prerequisites for justified TODO tests; do not claim deferred behavior is implemented. Distinguish source inspection from commands actually executed. Write a JSON report containing reviewer, report, and requested_edits. Leave requested_edits empty only when every aspect is accounted for and no edits are needed. Otherwise list concrete changes, including missing tests or justified TODO tests with prerequisite comments. Run cargo meta review record ANCHOR REPORT_FILE to finish. After edits or stale-input rejection, run cargo meta review start ANCHOR and review the fresh inputs. The gate fails until a current report with no requested edits is recorded. Dependency capture is agent-declared.
coordinator_instructions:
Follow sage-review-checklist for only the assigned anchor. Begin fresh review using cargo meta review start ANCHOR --instructions /tmp/ci-anchor-review-instructions.txt. Inspect current claim, implementation, complete tests, and capture dependencies through review read. Independently assess current evidence; do not transplant old approvals. Preserve justified TODO/N/A entries honestly. Record a complete claim-specific report. Coordinate all source edits with root BEFORE editing, to avoid invalidating concurrent reviews. Prefer reporting concrete necessary changes for root to batch; do not add unrelated evidence. You own only your assigned validation directory and unique /tmp report. Distinguish source inspection from tests executed. Do not commit.
Root centrally runs relevant suites. Do not repeat full suites for a source-only review unless investigating a specific concern. Report source assessment honestly without claiming execution. This does not waive regression reproduction for suspected bugs.

**Expansion returns direct module members, not a visible-name environment.** The result preserves deterministic order and provenance for source and generated direct items. Child-module members remain in the child, while imports and namespace lookup are interpreted later by resolution.

**Exhaustive absence requires complete expansion.** Published symbols are safe to use even when expansion is incomplete, but an omitted symbol supports a definite negative answer only when expansion is complete for that semantic question. This is the expansion consequence of [Incompleteness is an explicit terminal outcome](../../../rfds/architectural-foundations/README.md#incompleteness-is-an-explicit-terminal-outcome).

**Expansion observes expansion inputs, never checked semantic detail.** A module expansion may depend on parsed item identities, macro resolution and definitions, generated output, and completeness facts. It must not depend on item signatures, trait solutions, or function bodies.

**Parsing publishes syntax-backed identities, not semantic conclusions.** A represented item has stable local identity, self-contained CST, ordering, ownership, and provenance. Resolution and checking remain downstream operations, and malformed or unsupported top-level syntax is represented explicitly rather than accepted as a definition. Tree-sitter is temporary parser machinery under [Tree-sitter for parsing](../../../rfds/architectural-foundations/README.md#tree-sitter-for-parsing), not the published identity or syntax representation.

**Item identity is separate from tracked syntax detail.** Rebuilding a module may update an item's CST or absolute location without minting a new symbol when its semantic identity is unchanged. Every represented definition owns a separate CST stash so an equal sibling can be backdated independently. This applies [Symbols form the uniform semantic identity family](../../../rfds/architectural-foundations/README.md#symbols-form-the-uniform-semantic-identity-family) and [Stash for type-level interning](../../../rfds/architectural-foundations/README.md#stash-for-type-level-interning) at the parse boundary.

**Parse recovery never makes absence conclusive.** An error item or error CST node is terminal for the current parse, but any consumer asking an exhaustive question must treat the surrounding represented set as incomplete unless it can prove the error irrelevant to that question. This is the parsing consequence of [Incompleteness is an explicit terminal outcome](../../../rfds/architectural-foundations/README.md#incompleteness-is-an-explicit-terminal-outcome).

**The parse query depends only on parse inputs.** Parsing one module may read its source, scope, edition, compilation configuration, and generated parse source, but never resolved names, checked interfaces, bodies of other items, or trait results.

**Recursive expansion and same-module fixed points are distinct.** Recursive processing expands invocations emitted directly by another invocation. Salsa fixed-point recovery is used only when resolving a macro requires the provisional expanded members of that same module; convergence does not imply completeness.
## Incompleteness is an explicit terminal outcome
A phase or semantic subsystem distinguishes a complete result from a
conservative result limited by invalid or ambiguous source, unsupported Sage
functionality, unavailable external facts, or an explicit resource bound.
Such incompleteness is terminal for the current inputs and limits: continuing
to poll or schedule the same computation is not expected to make it complete.
An incomplete result may retain partial information for diagnostics or
conservative recovery, but it must identify which completeness guarantee is
absent and must not be presented as a successful complete value. Resource
exhaustion and ambiguity also remain distinct from a logical negative answer.
